$comment: Performance budgets. Baselines are first measurements; a check fails when a value regresses past its section's allowedRegression, and a section without a baseline is reported, not failed. openingFrameTime: just perf-opening (record with: just perf-opening record), headless Chromium since #48 (ADR 0144): its frames come on a 60 Hz clock, so p50 and p95 read 16.7 ms while the onboarding frame keeps up, against WebKit's 17 and 18. startup, idleMemory, inputLatency: just perf-app on the CEF desk, nightly in the e2e workflow's perf job; their baselines come from the CI runner (just perf-app record, or budgets.json from the job's artifact), and none was recorded on the Tauri app, so the CEF desk's first run sets them. targetMs are RT-16's targets, printed beside the values, not gates. compose, composeStartup, surfaceStartup, surfaceMemory, inputToPaint, deskAtRest: just perf-compositor (#58, e2e/perf/lib/compositor.ts) on the reference machine (docs/qa/TESTING.md); each section says why in its reason. budgetMs is a budget the value stays under, allowedRegression an allowance past a baseline, band a share either side of one; a baseline recorded on another platform or with another tool, and a budget on a software adapter, are reported, never failed.

compose.reason: #32 §3: composing 15 live surfaces at 1440p within 4 ms leaves 12 of a 60 Hz frame's 16.7 ms to the engine's paints and the shell. Gated on the p95 frame of cargo bench -p desk-compositor --bench compose (every window moved and every texture repainted each frame, so every frame is a full redraw; animate, compose and GPU done), on a GPU; a software adapter (lavapipe, WARP) reports it. p95Ms and medianMs are the reference machine's, kept for the trend.

composeStartup.reason: The compositor's own start, which every desk start waits for before it shows anything: from asking for a GPU device to the first composed frame of the compose budget's desk with the GPU done (device, pipelines, the machine's fonts, 15 textures uploaded, the first glyphs). The same bench run's median of three starts after one that warms what the OS and the driver keep for a new binary (a fresh build's first start took 4 times as long). Fails past the allowance on the platform its baseline was recorded on; the desk's whole start is surfaceStartup's.

surfaceStartup.reason: The desk's start to the first composed frame holding a web surface's paint, the median of ten starts in a row after one that takes the OS's first look at a newly laid out bundle (3.6 s against 0.2 s); the slowest of the ten is judged against the same baseline and allowance, so one stalled start fails, and is kept beside it (slowestMs). Until #112 two starts in five spent 1.4 s more before the desk's main ran, busy machine or quiet: Chromium's code-sign clone hard-linked the executable at every start, so macOS's exec policy took it for a new binary and scanned it again; the shell turns the clone off, and #58 had taken the fastest of five. Starts whose CEF took over a second are counted in stalls. The CEF desk in compositor mode through its surface probe (apps/desk/shell/tests/budgets.rs), started by the test, so the process's start, CEF's, a renderer's, the page's first paint, its import and a compose all count. #35 measured 137 to 248 ms from CreateBrowser to the first paint alone. Fails past the allowance on the platform its baseline was recorded on.

surfaceMemory.page: the PoC's light page, animating, 800x600 at scale 2, composed at 1920x1080
surfaceMemory.source: #35 (spikes/compositor/README.md): 916 MiB for the whole process tree with 1 light surface, 2,002 MiB with 10, so (2,002 - 916) / 9 a surface
surfaceMemory.reason: What one more live surface costs the machine, the number the live budget (ADR 0142: visible windows and the 8 most recent) is set from: the process tree's physical footprint with 1 and with 10 animating light surfaces, the difference per surface, as #35 measured it (apps/desk/shell/tests/budgets.rs). Within 20 % of #35's either way: above means a surface costs more than the live budget assumed; below means the baseline is stale or the surfaces did not render. RSS on Linux and Windows is reported until #61 records their baselines. Since #111 (ADR 0152) every surface renders on the desk's frame clock (external begin frames): 121.1 to 130 MiB a surface on the reference machine, where #52's internal begin frames read 162 to 191 (179.5 on main the same day), the GPU process holding about 60 MiB a surface more; on Chromium's full pipeline (#117, ADR 0157) 117.5 to 119.7. #35's baseline stays: this is the number the live budget was set from.

inputToPaint.reason: RT-16, input to screen within 16 ms, on the compositor's input path (#56): a press sent to a surface as the router sends it (pointer.down and pointer.up), twenty times beside two animating surfaces, through the surface probe (apps/desk/shell/tests/budgets.rs). Two gates: the press to the surface's next paint reaching the compositor, p95 (p95Ms, what the engine and the import cost), and to the desk's first composed frame holding it, median (frameP50Ms). The frame waits for the desk's own 60 Hz clock, so its p95 is the paint's plus up to a frame, 19 to 24 ms here, and is kept for the trend (frameP95Ms) rather than gated; RT-16's 16 ms at p95 would need a compose on damage, not on the clock. Since #111 (ADR 0152) a surface renders only on the desk's begin frames, and each step of a paint (the renderer's frame, the display's draw, the capture) waits for one: a press on an idle surface brings begin frames every 1 ms from the press until its paint. Since #117 (ADR 0157) Chromium runs its full pipeline, so a begin frame an idle page had nothing to draw for no longer holds the next ones back for a whole frame (CEF sends none while one is out), the one press in ten #111 saw wait a frame. The values are #117's median run of five at a load average of 5 to 8: the paint's p95 read 4.9 to 9.2 ms and the frame's median 13.5 to 14.7, where main read 9.4 to 14.2 and 15.2 to 15.8 in three runs the same hour (#111 read 12.1 to 22.3 and 13.9 to 17.9 on a busier machine). Since #129 (ADR 0159) five more presses are caught on purpose by CEF's busy-wait (a task delayed 5 ms after the press and CEF's work run at once, so that call loops out its 10 ms slice, as Chromium's own timers make one do now and then): gated, their paint's wait after the busy-wait ends, the median (caughtWaitMs within caughtWaitBudgetMs), since the frame clock's begin frames go out from a stand-in thread meanwhile and CEF's busy-wait runs them; kept for the trend, the press to that paint (caughtPaintP50Ms, at least the slice's 10 ms, as the desk's event loop waits for the call). #129's five runs at a load average of 8 to 13: the wait 0.01 to 0.04 ms, the press to the paint 10.7 to 11.4; main's pump read 4.1 to 5.0 ms and 13.7 to 16.4 in the probe. The twenty presses read 5.3 to 12.2 ms at p95 (two of them caught by chance in the 12.2) and 13.0 to 15.5 at the frame's median.

deskAtRest.reason: #129 (ADR 0159): what a desk at rest costs, through the surface probe's rest run (apps/desk/shell/tests/budgets.rs): three still surfaces, shown and awake, each long idle (ADR 0157), and the probe's loop run for ten seconds as the compositor window's event loop runs (a turn, then a wait for CEF's next work, the clock's next look or CEF's ask). Gated: the loop's wake-ups a second (each turn of the event loop) within wakeupsBudget, where main's pump woke 54.6 to 57.7 times (its poll every 33 ms whatever the clock did) and this change 33.2 to 38.3; and the browser process's CPU within cpuBudgetPercent of a core (0.8 to 1.9 % here, 1.2 to 2.1 with main's pump). Kept for the trend: the browser process's OS wake-ups (macOS proc_pid_rusage: 30.7 to 31.0 a second, 50.5 to 50.8 with main's pump), CEF's work calls a second, and the median paint of five presses, each on a surface long idle again (8 to 25 ms on main and here alike, against 5 ms on one idle under a second: not explained by #129). Most of what still wakes a desk at rest is CEF's answers to the slow clock's begin frames, ten a second a long-idle surface. The values are #129's median run of five at a load average of 8 to 13.
